plan: This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding above my value risks overpaying, while bidding below reduces my chance of winning profitable auctions. With a value of $29, the optimal action is to bid exactly $29 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors, since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own) if you win. Overbidding risks winning at a price above value, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With no repeated learning needed since values are redrawn independently, the optimal strategy is straightforward: bid exactly my private value of $30.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid up or down. Bidding above value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $6, the optimal bid is exactly $6.
